net sales.text:

Residential And SMB - Glo Fiber Expansio.heading: Residential & SMB - Glo Fiber Expansion Markets revenue
Residential And SMB - Glo Fiber Expansio.text:

Residential And SMB - Incumbent Broadban.heading: Residential & SMB - Incumbent Broadband Markets revenue
Residential And SMB - Incumbent Broadban.text:
Revenue from residential and small and medium business (“SMB”) customers in Incumbent Broadband Markets are primarily earned through the Company’s provision of data, video and voice services over primarily hybrid fiber coaxial (“HFC”) cable and to a lesser extent fiber to the home (“FTTH”) networks in incumbent markets.

Residential & SMB - Incumbent Broadband Markets revenue increased by $0.6 million, or 0.3%, in the year ended December 31, 2024 as compared with the year ended December 31, 2023 primarily due to $5.6 million of revenues earned in the newly acquired Horizon markets. These revenues were offset by a $5.0 million decline in the legacy Shentel markets due to lower video revenue from a 16.9% decline in video revenue generating units (“RGUs”) and a 1.6% decline in data RGUs with the majority of the decline due to the end of the ACP program.

Commercial Fiber.heading: Commercial Fiber revenue
Commercial Fiber.text:
Shentel’s Commercial Fiber revenue is primarily earned through the Company’s provision of high-speed Ethernet, wavelength, dark fiber leasing and managed services over fiber optic networks to commercial customers.

Commercial Fiber revenue increased by $24.9 million, or 59.1%, in the year ended December 31, 2024 as compared with the year ended December 31, 2023 due to $30.7 million of revenues earned in the newly acquired Horizon markets, and partially offset by a $5.8 million decline in legacy Shentel markets as a result of the previously disclosed T-Mobile backhaul revenue churn associated with the decommissioning of the former Sprint network.

Residential And SMB - Glo Fiber Expansio.heading: Residential & SMB - Glo Fiber Expansion Markets revenue
Residential And SMB - Glo Fiber Expansio.text:
Revenue from residential and SMB customers in Glo Fiber Expansion Markets are primarily earned through the Company’s provision of data, video and voice services over FTTH networks in new greenfield expansion markets.

Residential & SMB - Glo Fiber Expansion Markets revenue increased by $22.8 million, or 65.0%, in the year ended December 31, 2024 as compared with the year ended December 31, 2023 due to a $21.4 million increase in legacy Shentel markets and $1.4 million of revenues earned in the newly acquired Horizon markets. The increase in legacy Shentel markets revenue was primarily due to 50.9% year-over-year growth in data RGUs associated with the Company’s investment in expanded geographies for Glo Fiber and a 7.3% increase in data average revenue per unit (“ARPU”).

RLEC & Other.heading: RLEC & Other revenue
RLEC & Other.text:
Shentel’s RLEC & Other revenue is primarily earned through the Company’s provision of voice and DSL telephone services over copper networks primarily in Shenandoah County, Virginia and Ross County, Ohio. Shentel also earns governmental support revenue through the federal USF.

RLEC & Other revenue increased by $10.6 million, or 70.8%, in the year ended December 31, 2024 as compared with the year ended December 31, 2023 due to $10.1 million of revenues earned in the newly acquired Horizon markets and an increase in governmental support revenue.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
